metadata.note: Gainesville Midland Railway (Gainesville - Athens, with the Monroe Branch Belmont - Monroe) and its 3 ft gauge predecessor the Gainesville, Jefferson and Southern Railroad (Gainesville - Social Circle and the Belmont - Jefferson branch), Georgia. Rule 4 split at the 5 Jul 1904 foreclosure sale (GM incorporated Aug 1904): GJ&S features and GM features share the Gainesville - Belmont stem and the Belmont - Jefferson and Belmont - Monroe geometry, in their own colours. NOT splits: Georgia Railroad lessees' stock control of the GJ&S from 1883; GJ&S receivership 1897-1904; GM receivership 1921-c.1926; the 1926-27 Seaboard purchase agreement (apparently never consummated; SAL bought the road in 1959, after passenger service). Monroe - Social Circle (ex-Walton RR) left the road in 1904 for the Georgia Railroad and has no GM feature.
sources: Savannah Morning News 1898-10-29, image 9 (Chronicling America; found via loc.gov full-text search, as quoted in the research report)
Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 issue (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt): Gainesville Midland entry, July 1951, 'FREIGHT SERVICE ONLY'
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) and OpenHistoricalMap, 2026-11-09, traced with opstrace.py. The 1-degree railtrace tile over east Atlanta repeatedly timed out on the mirror, so the scratch script read the same railway ways as 0.25-degree tiles (separately cached; the shared 1-degree cache was not touched). The road is NOT tagged old_railway_operator=Gainesville Midland: an old_railway_operator probe (Gainesville|Midland|GM|Seaboard|SAL|Jefferson) found only SAL-tagged ways. The live line is tagged name='Gainesville-Midland Subdivision', old_railway_operator=SAL, note:old_railway_operator='Gainesville Midland' (CSX, railway_milepost GGM); the Gainesville end survives as the 'Midland Greenway' rail-trail; the lifted Monroe Branch is mapped as railway=abandoned ways named 'Gainesville Midland Winder Branch' (Winder - Sells, plus two short fragments near Thurmack) and 'Gainesville Midland Monroe Branch' (Winder - north edge of Monroe). A scratch Operator subclass therefore matched name= and note:old_railway_operator= as well, and costed SAL / Monroe Railroad / Great Walton ways as successor track (1.25x). fetch_gap over Belmont - Winder, Winder - Monroe and Monroe - Social Circle: OHM has a continuous GJ&S/GM grade (start_date 1889) Belmont - Winder - Monroe and the ex-Walton line Monroe - Social Circle (start_date 1881); OSM has the live Great Walton Railroad (old_railway_operator 'Monroe Railroad;Georgia') Monroe - Social Circle. Geocodes checked by type: Gainesville, Talmo, Jefferson, Athens, Braselton, Winder, Bethlehem, Monroe, Social Circle returned the places themselves (administrative), Candler and Oconee Heights hamlets; 'Klondike, Georgia' returned a DeKalb County hamlet (wrong place, not used); no county answers. Pinned by hand: Gainesville terminus at the Midland Greenway north end (34.2957,-83.8266); Belmont at the GM line beside Belmont hamlet (34.1865,-83.7636); Hoschton at the Hoschton Train Depot on Railroad Avenue (34.0973,-83.7617); Sells at the north end of the mapped Winder Branch grade (34.0625,-83.7203); Monroe at the north end of the Great Walton track (33.7916,-83.7111). Fowler Junction was not pinned; the GM-named track ends at 33.9725,-83.4073 and the trace runs on to Athens over ex-SAL/untagged track. Simplified douglas_peucker(8 m) then trim_reversals; spurs() empty on every feature.
metadata.colour_choice: Neither company had a feature anywhere in data/ (grep for 'Gainesville Midland', 'Gainesville, Jefferson'). Both colours chosen by a script that scored HSV candidates by their distance from all 858 colours already in data/ and took the most distant: Gainesville Midland #4B3AA5, Gainesville, Jefferson and Southern #66A53A (each >20 RGB units from every existing colour, and far from each other). Verified programmatically after writing that every feature with each company string carries an identical colour.
tracer_decisions: Drawn exactly the report's drawable spans: [1]+[3]+[4]+[5] GJ&S Gainesville - Social Circle 1886-1898 OPEN (one feature, identical spans); [2] Jefferson Branch 1886-1895 OPEN; [6] GM Gainesville - Athens 1906-1924 OPEN, drawn once ([9]/[10] not drawn separately); [7] Belmont - Winder 1918-1921 OPEN; [8] Winder - Monroe 1921 ANCHOR.
The Monroe Branch north feature starts at Belmont, not Gainesville, because the Gainesville - Belmont stem is already drawn 1906-1924 by the main line feature.
The Fowler Junction - Athens trackage-rights leg is coloured Gainesville Midland because GM ran the trains over it; the track owner (Seaboard) is noted, not split.
No Seaboard-coloured feature: the report's inference that SAL never operated the GM before 1959 is followed; see not_yet_sourced.
not_yet_sourced: PASSENGER END (all lines): confirmed only to July 1924 (Gainesville - Athens), 1921 (Monroe Branch). 1929 probable (RailGa-listed 1929 Official Guide and Russell's timetables, images unviewable); 1940-45 Athens Banner-Herald 'MIDLAND Passenger' hits are a lead only (unread, could be bus/motor car); 1946 per Hanson, uncited; July 1951 Official Guide: 'FREIGHT SERVICE ONLY'. All end years on this layer are [OPEN].
GJ&S 1899-1904 and GM 1904-1905: very probably passenger trains ran across the 1904 change of owner, but nothing found proves it; not bridged.
GJ&S 1883-1885: line open from 1883/84; first passenger timetable listed 1886.
Jefferson Branch: whether the 1886/1888/1895 GJ&S timetables show it is unverified (images not viewed).

1926-27 SEABOARD DEAL: ICC approved SAL acquisition 24 Oct 1927 ('The Seaboard will operate the portion of the road from Gainesville to Fowler Junction') vs Hanson (SAL backed out when the Monroe abandonment was refused). The 1951 Guide lists an independent Gainesville Midland Railroad; if SAL did operate Gainesville - Athens from c.1928, a Seaboard-coloured feature would be needed - but no passenger year after 1924 is drawn, so the question does not yet affect the map.
GAUGE CONFLICT: Gainesville - Jefferson widened 1906 (Savannah Tribune 15 Sep 1906, contemporary) vs 1908 (RailGa, Hanson). Belmont - Monroe widened 1913.
OPENING CONFLICT: Hoschton - Jug Tavern Sept 1883 (RailGa) vs Hoschton - Monroe 11 Mar 1884 (ICC); Belmont - Jefferson 'soon followed' (RailGa) vs 1 Jun 1883 (ICC).
Corporate sequence 1926-1933 (sale to bondholders 1926 per Hanson vs receivers still in 1933 RFC list; Railway -> Railroad renaming date).
NRHS Atlanta excursions behind GM decapods (1950s): route and dates unknown; not drawn.

ALIGNMENT Belmont - Hoschton - Sells: OHM and two OSM fragments map the Monroe Branch grade 3 km east of Braselton and the Hoschton depot, leaving the GM line east of Belmont; the layer draws straight lines through Belmont and the Hoschton depot instead (see the Monroe Branch geometry_quality). A USGS topographic map of c.1900-1945 would settle it.
Headways and avg_speed_kmh are estimates throughout.
omitted: Gainesville - New Holland branch (1.75 mi, GM-built): no passenger evidence; freight/industrial, also the start of the Gainesville & Northwestern's trackage rights. Excluded (Rule 1).
Gainesville & Northwestern (Gainesville - Helen): a separate company, not a predecessor. Not drawn here.
Gainesville Midland 1951-1959 and SAL/SCL/CSX after 1959: freight only (Rule 1).
Monroe - Social Circle under the Georgia Railroad (Monroe Railroad) after 1904: not this road; freight only by 1951; passenger years not researched.
Walton Railroad (Monroe - Social Circle, 5 ft, before 1884): not researched.
metadata.freight_only_excluded: Whole Gainesville Midland after an unknown passenger end before July 1951 (Official Guide Feb 1952: 'FREIGHT SERVICE ONLY'); the New Holland branch; everything after 1959.

properties.geometry_quality: Gainesville - Social Circle: traced 48.6 mi against a documented 52 mi (RailGa); ICC pieces c.10 (stem) + 34.22 (Belmont - Monroe) + c.10 (Monroe - Social Circle) = c.54 mi. Straight-line legs (approximations): Belmont - Hoschton depot 6.2 mi; Hoschton depot - Sells 3.4 mi; end of the mapped GM Monroe Branch grade (33.807,-83.723) - Monroe (Great Walton track, 33.7916,-83.7111) 1.3 mi. Drawn length by OSM source: Gainesville Midland 28.2 mi, (straight line) 10.8 mi, Monroe Railroad;Georgia 9.7 mi. LATER-ALIGNMENT NOTE (Rule 2): this 3 ft gauge era (to 1906/08 on Gainesville - Jefferson, to 1913 on Belmont - Monroe) is drawn on the later standard-gauge alignment as it survives in OSM (live CSX Gainesville Midland Subdivision, abandoned grade, or rail-trail). The narrow-gauge line was widened in place per the ICC valuation and RailGa, but local realignments at widening were not checked. HOSCHTON ALIGNMENT CONFLICT: the only mapped grade north of Sells - OpenHistoricalMap's GJ&S/GM way (Belmont-area junction 34.1837,-83.7428 - Thurmack - Sells) and two OSM abandoned fragments named 'Gainesville Midland Winder Branch' near Thurmack (34.12-34.15, -83.73) - runs 3 km EAST of Braselton and of the Hoschton Train Depot on Railroad Avenue (34.0973,-83.7617), and leaves the GM line 2 km east of Belmont hamlet. The report and RailGa put the fork at Belmont and the 1883 depot at Hoschton, so this layer does NOT follow that grade: it draws Belmont - Hoschton depot (6.2 mi, passing within 0.1 km of Braselton) and Hoschton depot - Sells (3.4 mi) as STRAIGHT-LINE approximations, then the mapped GM grade Sells - Winder. Which is right (a moved depot / mis-mapped grade, or a later bypass) is not resolved. Into Monroe the last 1.3 mi of the mapped GM grade is likewise a straight line. Gainesville - Belmont is the common stem shared with the Jefferson Branch and the Gainesville Midland main line; Monroe - Social Circle is the ex-Walton Railroad (5 ft, converted to 3 ft in 1884), which passed to the Georgia Railroad (Monroe Railroad) in 1904 and is drawn on the live Great Walton Railroad track (OSM old_railway_operator 'Monroe Railroad;Georgia'; OHM start_date 1881). Waypoint offsets from the line (km): Gainesville GM terminus 0.0, Candler 0.0, Belmont 0.0, Sells 0.0, Winder 0.0, Bethlehem 0.1, Monroe 0.0, Social Circle 0.6.

segments.note: [OPEN] Gainesville - Candler - Belmont - Braselton - Hoschton - Jug Tavern (Winder) - Bethlehem - Monroe - Social Circle, the GJ&S main line (report blocks [1],[3],[4],[5]); 3 ft gauge, steam (no animal era - Rule 5). Start 1886 = the earliest GJ&S passenger timetable RailGa lists (1886, 1888 and 1895 timetables listed; images not viewed). The line opened Gainesville - Hoschton 1883 and through to Monroe/Social Circle by 11 Mar 1884 (ICC valuation; RailGa has Jug Tavern Sept 1883 - SOURCE CONFLICT), very probably with passengers, but the sources say only 'opened', so 1883-85 is not drawn. End 1898 = the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end: Savannah Morning News, 29 Oct 1898, 'New cars have been put on the Gainesville, Jefferson and Southern Railroad, between here and Social Circle ... doing good business both of passenger hauling and freight.' Service very probably ran to the 5 Jul 1904 foreclosure sale, but nothing found proves 1899-1904. Do not extend without evidence. Receivership from Mar 1897 and Georgia Railroad lessees' stock control from 1883 are not operator changes. Headway is an estimate (one round trip a day assumed), not sourced.

Headway NOT sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Gainesville - Athens: traced 39.6 mi against a documented c.40-42 mi (RailGa '40-mile line'; 1926 Evening Star 42 mi; ICC Gainesville - Jefferson 20.00 + Jefferson - Fowler Jct 16.28 = 36.28 mi plus c.2 mi SAL trackage rights = c.38.3; CSX Gainesville Midland Subdivision today 38.3 mi). NO straight-line legs. Drawn length by OSM source: Gainesville Midland 38.2 mi, (untagged) 0.9 mi, SAL 0.6 mi. Gainesville - Fowler Junction drawn on the live CSX Gainesville Midland Subdivision (and the Midland Greenway rail-trail at the Gainesville end); the GM-named track ends at 33.9725,-83.4073, taken here as Fowler Junction (not pinned from a source), and the last 1.5 mi into Athens runs on ex-SAL (0.6 mi) and untagged (0.9 mi) track - the report gives c.2 mi of SAL trackage rights. Gainesville - Jefferson is the ex-GJ&S alignment widened in place; any realignment at the 1906/08 widening was not checked. The Athens terminus is pinned at the city, not at a sourced GM passenger stop (GM shared the SAL freight depot; its passenger station is not established). Waypoint offsets from the line (km): Gainesville GM terminus 0.0, Candler 0.0, Belmont 0.0, Talmo 0.0, Jefferson 0.8, Oconee Heights 0.1, Athens 0.9.

segments.note: [OPEN] Gainesville - Candler - Belmont - Talmo - Jefferson - Fowler Junction - Oconee Heights - Athens (report block [6]; [9]+[10] are its two halves and are not drawn separately). Start 1906: Savannah Tribune 15 Sep 1906 - first broad-gauge train through to Jefferson 'last Saturday, and in a short time will put trains through to Athens'; exact Athens opening date not found. Gainesville - Jefferson under the GM 1904-05 (narrow gauge) is not proven and not drawn. Last ~2 mi Fowler Junction - Athens over the Seaboard Air Line by trackage rights (RailGa). Further evidence: 1921 employees' offer to 'keep trains moving' and cut 'freight and passenger rates' (Atlanta Tri-Weekly Journal 29 Sep 1921); 1923 receivers' petition to end 'both passenger and freight service' Belmont - Athens (not carried out); 22 Jul 1924 bus petition: 'no immediate interference with passenger schedules' Athens - Gainesville. End 1924 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end - 1929 probable (RailGa-listed 1929 Official Guide/Russell's timetables, unviewed), 1946 per Hanson (uncited), freight only by July 1951 (Official Guide). Do not extend without evidence. Receivership from Feb 1921 is not an operator change. Mixed trains and motor cars in later years (Hanson) - still rail passenger service. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: Savannah Tribune 15 Sep 1906 (start); Atlanta Tri-Weekly Journal 29 Sep 1921, 14 Jul 1923 and 22 Jul 1924 (continuation and the 1924 last confirmed year); RailGa for the Fowler Jct - Athens trackage rights (as quoted in research/branches/gainesville_midland_railway.txt, researched 2026-11-09; the tracer did not re-open these pages). Headway NOT sourced.

Belmont - Monroe was abandoned 1947-48; Sells - Winder is on the OSM abandoned way 'Gainesville Midland Winder Branch'. Waypoint offsets from the line (km): Sells 0.0, Winder 0.0.

segments.note: [OPEN] Belmont - Braselton - Hoschton - Winder, north part of the GM Monroe Branch (report block [7]); trains ran through from Gainesville over the common stem. 1918: 'a passenger car on a train going south on the Gainesville Midland railroad turned over near here [Winder]', 28 Jan 1918, eleven hurt (Atlanta Semi-Weekly Journal 1 Feb 1918). 1921: system-wide employees' offer to keep trains running and cut passenger rates (Atlanta Tri-Weekly Journal 29 Sep 1921) - if that system-wide item is rejected, this collapses to 1918 alone. 1904-1917 not proven (1909 and 1913 items show trains running, passengers not stated) and not drawn. End 1921 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end; the branch survived to its 1947-48 abandonment, which is NOT the passenger end. Do not extend without evidence. 3 ft gauge until 1913. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) and OpenHistoricalMap, 2026-11-09, traced with opstrace.py. The 1-degree railtrace tile over east Atlanta repeatedly timed out on the mirror, so the scratch script read the same railway ways as 0.25-degree tiles (separately cached; the shared 1-degree cache was not touched). The road is NOT tagged old_railway_operator=Gainesville Midland: an old_railway_operator probe (Gainesville|Midland|GM|Seaboard|SAL|Jefferson) found only SAL-tagged ways. The live line is tagged name='Gainesville-Midland Subdivision', old_railway_operator=SAL, note:old_railway_operator='Gainesville Midland' (CSX, railway_milepost GGM); the Gainesville end survives as the 'Midland Greenway' rail-trail; the lifted Monroe Branch is mapped as railway=abandoned ways named 'Gainesville Midland Winder Branch' (Winder - Sells, plus two short fragments near Thurmack) and 'Gainesville Midland Monroe Branch' (Winder - north edge of Monroe). A scratch Operator subclass therefore matched name= and note:old_railway_operator= as well, and costed SAL / Monroe Railroad / Great Walton ways as successor track (1.25x). fetch_gap over Belmont - Winder, Winder - Monroe and Monroe - Social Circle: OHM has a continuous GJ&S/GM grade (start_date 1889) Belmont - Winder - Monroe and the ex-Walton line Monroe - Social Circle (start_date 1881); OSM has the live Great Walton Railroad (old_railway_operator 'Monroe Railroad;Georgia') Monroe - Social Circle. Geocodes checked by type: Gainesville, Talmo, Jefferson, Athens, Braselton, Winder, Bethlehem, Monroe, Social Circle returned the places themselves (administrative), Candler and Oconee Heights hamlets; 'Klondike, Georgia' returned a DeKalb County hamlet (wrong place, not used); no county answers. Pinned by hand: Gainesville terminus at the Midland Greenway north end (34.2957,-83.8266); Belmont at the GM line beside Belmont hamlet (34.1865,-83.7636); Hoschton at the Hoschton Train Depot on Railroad Avenue (34.0973,-83.7617); Sells at the north end of the mapped Winder Branch grade (34.0625,-83.7203); Monroe at the north end of the Great Walton track (33.7916,-83.7111). Fowler Junction was not pinned; the GM-named track ends at 33.9725,-83.4073 and the trace runs on to Athens over ex-SAL/untagged track. Simplified douglas_peucker(8 m) then trim_reversals; spurs() empty on every feature.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Winder - Bethlehem - Monroe, south part of the GM Monroe Branch (report block [8]). 1921 is the one year with any passenger evidence, and that evidence is system-wide: the GM employees' Sept 1921 offer to keep the receivership road's trains moving and cut 'freight and passenger rates' 20% (Atlanta Tri-Weekly Journal 29 Sep 1921; Cordele Dispatch 28 Sep 1921). Service certainly ran wider both ways - the line was in GM hands 1904-1947/48 and 1923 press describes the road as operating 'Gainesville to Monroe, via Winder and Belmont' - but no other year is confirmed for this section. Never widen an anchor to look plausible; remove it only if system-wide evidence is rejected. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.
